purpose: Whole-library performance, memory, algorithm and API audit; experiments and recommendations, no library implementation changes.

scope.method: Static inventory of every Blot module, complete existing benchmark catalog, manual review of selected hot paths and mechanisms, review of all five standalone shaders, and paired experimental probes. Not a line-by-line correctness proof of every function.

measurementLimits: Timings include fixture construction, guest call and result decoding. They are isolated native workloads, not gdev frame-time gains.
Committed bytes are reusable Wasm arena capacity, not live heap size or process RSS. Ownership counters describe one extra untimed call.
Largest-size ratios are not universal speedups. Prototype restrictions are part of each finding.
Scaling exponents are empirical over the recorded sizes; width-based navigation/terrain and output-sensitive collision workloads need their proper dimension.
handles-dense-churn includes a quadratic application reference-remapping baseline; it does not establish quadratic handle lookup.
Relation-index construction loses to scanning at 16 uses in the baseline but wins at 128; include build cost when choosing indices.

Library source hashes stayed unchanged throughout the audit. Baseline and final probes have the same compiler binary hash, but different native runner/config hashes because probes and counters were added.

findings.problem: One message goes through write_many, dirty-index preparation, and a full page-table traversal.
findings.recommendation: Implement a validated single-write path using pages.push/set, an empty-batch no-op, then evaluate radix paging for larger logs.
findings.limits: Prototype assumes valid epochs, sufficient sequence space, and U32 payloads. Production must retain overflow/reset semantics. Workload writes twice the retention capacity and reads the retained tail.

findings.problem: Persistent HAMT construction and lookup perform substantial node allocation/reference-count work for tables that never change after construction.
findings.recommendation: Offer a separate builder/frozen open-addressed table for read-heavy data. Keep persistent maps for cheap forks and edits; investigate a bulk HAMT builder and structural set algebra separately.
findings.limits: Build plus four lookup passes, not lookup alone. Prototype supports U32 keys/values, full-width keys, separate occupancy, load <= 0.5, and no persistent edit API. Memory is committed guest arena capacity.

findings.evidence: paired prototype using existing sparse iteration
findings.problem: A rare With query traverses all occupied entity words, interprets filters/source lookup per word, then scans all 32 bits twice. Cache lookup still validates sources and allocates a recursive fingerprint.
findings.recommendation: Bind filters to source indices once, retain occupied-word lists, choose the rarest mandatory positive anchor, intersect words and enumerate set bits. Preserve fallback semantics for Any/Without/Optional and cache lineage.
findings.limits: 64 matching components in 65,536 live entities, 32 uncached selections, including setup. Anchored case uses ecs.indices; it is not a complete generic query planner. Cached steady membership is already a separate supported path.

findings.problem: handles.encode repeatedly concatenates the entire growing word output for slots and framed values.
findings.recommendation: Provide encoded_length plus encode_into or an owned append builder, and cursor/span decoding to avoid per-field slices. Use it in handles and assess other codecs individually.
findings.limits: Exact writer prototype only handles a dense never-deleted U32 store. Production must cover arbitrary codecs, free/retired slots and overflow. Existing codec.sequence_encode uses a different collector and was not shown to have this same cost.

findings.evidence: paired prototype plus differential malformed-input test
findings.problem: Complete flame decoding exhibits quadratic retain/release traffic while hot aggregation and layout are approximately linear in these probes.
findings.recommendation: Validate and index numeric packet offsets first, then generate reference-bearing records once. Investigate equivalent compiler ownership optimization for early-failure loops.
findings.limits: Complete-packet contract only, not flame_prefix. Differential checks cover valid Unicode payloads, every prefix, and malformed values at each position. Timing packet has empty names. Exact compiler root cause is not established.

findings.problem: Entity count is historical high-water, IDs are never reused, despawn only clears live bits, and component payloads remain stored unless separately removed. Maybe component storage also duplicates occupancy and can prevent packed numeric payload storage.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit structural cleanup with typed component hooks; then design generational reusable slots or explicit compaction/remapping. Separate occupancy masks from numeric payloads. Offer dense/sparse storage choices before considering archetype chunks.
findings.limits: Changing plain U32 IDs requires a stale-reference and fork-lineage contract. Existing retained snapshots must remain valid. This is not a measured memory leak diagnosis for gdev.

findings.evidence: source inspection; single-write probe supports local fast path only
findings.problem: Flat page tables still require copying/traversing the whole outer array; spatial.refit copies the entire bounds buffer even for one changed item. Paged render collection can still scan historical slots.
findings.recommendation: Use a persistent wide-radix page directory above a measured size threshold, batch all edits to each leaf, short-circuit no-op changes, and retain explicit live/dirty indices for collection. Evaluate paged spatial bounds or caller-owned scratch for refits.
findings.limits: Extra indirection can lose for small arrays; benchmark retained snapshots and batch sizes. Existing ECS columns already have multiple levels, so this is not a recommendation to add their existing structure again.

findings.evidence: measured scaling plus source inspection; replacement unmeasured
findings.problem: Each A* query initializes five arrays sized to every grid cell even when only two cells are expanded.
findings.recommendation: Explicit reusable scratch with generation stamps and bounded frontier storage; consider hierarchical routes for large worlds and shared reverse flow fields for common destinations.
findings.observation: Sixteen two-expansion queries on a 256x256 grid take 2.869 ms and 4,160 KiB committed memory. Scaling exponent 1.98 is versus width, hence proportional to grid area, despite fixed search work.
findings.limits: Timing includes grid construction; source inspection establishes repeated full-grid initialization. Reused scratch must remain caller-owned and preserve snapshot/replay semantics. No speedup estimate for a replacement.

findings.evidence: source inspection; benefit and edge-case behavior unmeasured
findings.problem: Wake propagation performs up to 32 complete scans of cached support contacts.
findings.recommendation: Build/reuse endpoint adjacency and process newly woken bodies once with a queue. Test reversed long chains, duplicates, removed bodies and deterministic ordering.
findings.limits: The fixed pass cap is also a correctness investigation for sufficiently long adversarial chains; no failing witness has been established in this audit. Adjacency construction can cost more for small contact sets.

findings.problem: Repeated queries can redo path validation/segment lengths, grid classification, graph preparation, or UI topology work.
findings.recommendation: Prepare immutable validated paths with cumulative lengths and binary search or a caller-owned cursor; retain grid cost classification; use adjacency/indegree queues for large dependency graphs; separate UI topology from dirty property evaluation.
findings.limits: Recipe/schedule planning is often cold. Do not replace small bounded scans without a workload showing amortization.

findings.evidence: source inspection and baseline scaling; replacement unmeasured
findings.problem: Per-item effectful declarations repeatedly fetch/write resources and append reference-bearing rows. Queue publication slices pending jobs and builds deliveries.
findings.recommendation: Expose bulk declaration/build/freeze APIs, collect sounds/voices/UI records once per phase, use head offsets or chunked queues when pending sets are large, and keep bounded trace history as a ring.
findings.limits: Sound/voice baseline is 0.758 ms at 256 declarations with observed exponent 1.63; this does not isolate each contributor. Small bounded services may remain simpler and faster as arrays.

findings.problem: Some callers need one quantile, a few best results, a Boolean, or 2D nearest data but pay for sorting/materializing larger or 3D results. Fixed point-grid bucket capacity may degrade as it grows.
findings.recommendation: Evaluate deterministic selection for one quantile, a heap for large top-k, visitor/any/closest spatial APIs, specialized 2D bounds, and explicit grid rehash/rebuild policy. Keep canonical sorted results as a separate contract.
findings.limits: Insertion top-k is appropriate for small k. Ordering and floating-point reduction order may be observable. Octrees are not automatically better for clustered floor-plane data.

findings.problem: Sound includes named music/effects/ambience/interface buses, default reverb sends, and host-oriented fade assumptions in the generic layer.
findings.recommendation: Keep generic audio records and builders pure; move named buses, initial mixes and fades into caller presets. Offer thin ECS adapters separately so mechanisms compose without requiring an ECS world.
findings.limits: This is API orthogonality and package-boundary cleanup, not a measured performance win. Keep Pen wire translation in the optional adapter.

findings.evidence: compiler timing instrumentation and source inspection
findings.problem: Fixture compilation and watched-tree hashing repeat across benchmark modules; the report also duplicates entire source inventories. Existing compile times are per fixture, not edit-to-rebuild latency.
findings.recommendation: Memoize source inventories within a run, deduplicate report inventories, and evaluate dependency-keyed artifact/session caching plus a focused developer watch command. Retain a full validation path and include compiler/settings/plugin/host identity in cache keys.
findings.limits: No incremental compiler speedup was measured. Audit archive deduplicates inventories losslessly; production benchmark report format was not changed to deduplicate.

findings.evidence: source inspection of all five shaders; no GPU timing
findings.problem: Mesh fragments normalize frame light direction and derive material constants; display fragments derive exposure gain. Some of these inputs are uniform.
findings.recommendation: If GPU profiling justifies it, supply validated normalized lighting/precomputed material constants and exposure gain, or provide specialized pipeline variants. Retain robust normal handling and HDR/extreme-value witnesses.
findings.limits: Drivers may already hoist work; visual tests are not performance measurements. Do not weaken numerical guards or change host-owned resources based on this audit.

languageRecommendations.workaround: Copy with array.generate before mutation instead of array.slice.
languageRecommendations.languageFix: Propagate exact freshness/alias provenance through slice/copy results and library wrappers.
languageRecommendations.counterEvidence: 4,099 destroyed objects versus 4; zero cycle passes in both.

languageRecommendations.workaround: Choose a scalar value conditionally, then perform one unconditional array write.
languageRecommendations.languageFix: Merge exclusive array ownership across control-flow arms and early exits; preserve private-loop updates through failable validation.
languageRecommendations.counterEvidence: 4,098 destroyed objects versus 2; zero cycle passes in both.

languageRecommendations.workaround: Flatten numeric records into scalar lanes in hot kernels; avoid reconstruction at helper boundaries.
languageRecommendations.languageFix: Cross-call scalar replacement, unboxed aggregate ABI and direct field views into packed rows; extend safe layout selection to occupied numeric component payloads.
languageRecommendations.limits: Current source already supports qualifying nested packed rows and allocation-aware inlining. Storage packing alone does not establish allocation-free row access. Nested workload 3.517 ms/832 KiB versus flat 1.334 ms/384 KiB.

languageRecommendations.evidence: source inspection and existing Ink workaround notes; not isolated here
languageRecommendations.workaround: Inline helpers, pass immediately invoked closures, hand-write scalar operations, or move all writes into one function.
languageRecommendations.languageFix: Precise noescape/borrow/fresh-result summaries across generic calls; diagnostics with source spans explaining why a value was copied, boxed, retained, or denied acyclic proof.
languageRecommendations.limits: Do not infer all historical workaround restrictions still apply to the installed compiler.

languageRecommendations.workaround: Manual pre-count/fill passes and flat scalar buffers.
languageRecommendations.languageFix: An ownership-checked builder or scoped edit capability with deterministic freeze; preserve functional APIs and immutable snapshot guarantees while permitting amortized construction.
languageRecommendations.limits: This is a design direction, not a request for unrestricted mutation or a hidden global allocator.

languageRecommendations.evidence: negative control plus local compiler source review
languageRecommendations.workaround: Avoid blanket syntactic bans; version workaround documentation against executable probes.
languageRecommendations.languageFix: Maintain optimization qualification tests by data shape/control flow, and expose missing proof reasons. Investigate remaining acyclic-proof gaps before changing cycle collection globally.
languageRecommendations.limits: Simple nested-array comprehension is approximately linear and has the same committed memory/destroyed-object count as generate. Local source already has immutable-acyclic proofs and an adaptive collector threshold; installed binary capabilities must be measured.

architecturalExperiments.detail: Persistent snapshots, transient construction, frozen read-mostly tables, dense numeric columns and sparse reference components need different representations behind clear APIs.
architecturalExperiments.measurement: Compare edit/read/snapshot mixes and allocation traffic; do not benchmark only steady lookup.

architecturalExperiments.idea: Compile queries and schemas into plans
architecturalExperiments.detail: Bind query sources, codec layouts, field-access masks and stable topology once. Consider static specialization for known schemas while retaining a dynamic fallback.
architecturalExperiments.measurement: Track compile time and code size as well as runtime; avoid specializing every tiny call site.

architecturalExperiments.detail: Treat queries, relations and render membership as caller-owned derived views fed by precise structural journals; choose rescan or incremental maintenance based on dirty fraction.
architecturalExperiments.measurement: Include journal/reset cost, fork invalidation, and high-churn cases.

architecturalExperiments.idea: Separate durable identity from hot storage identity
architecturalExperiments.detail: Use stable handles externally and compact phase-local indices internally, with explicit remapping at publish boundaries.
architecturalExperiments.measurement: Test stale IDs, rollback/forks, saves, compaction cost and working-set locality.

architecturalExperiments.idea: Publish immutable snapshots at explicit phase boundaries
architecturalExperiments.detail: Batch commands into an ownership-checked workspace, perform local edits, and freeze the result. Keep readers and previous snapshots isolated.
architecturalExperiments.measurement: Measure large retained histories as well as the common single-current-world case; no hidden state.

architecturalExperiments.idea: Select AoS/SoA/AoSoA layout without changing domain types
architecturalExperiments.detail: A compiler/storage-policy facility could keep idiomatic records while choosing columns or vector-width tiles for hot loops.
architecturalExperiments.measurement: Memory traffic, row extraction allocations, useful SIMD lane work, and API/code-size cost all matter.
